response.report:
EXAM: Chest radiograph, one view, 2026-11-21
CLINICAL INDICATION: Emergency department. Shortness of breath. History of prostate cancer on hormone therapy. Portable film.
ORDERING PROVIDER: Dr. J. Marte (synthetic), ED
COMPARISON: Chest radiograph, 2026-06-30. Note: the prior report reads 'PA chest. Heart size normal. Lungs clear.' with no cardiac device mentioned. The prior image shows an enlarged cardiac silhouette and a left chest wall cardiac device generator with transvenous leads. The radiologist should confirm that the prior report belongs to this prior image.
TECHNIQUE: Current is AP, labeled supine portable, with low lung volumes and mild rotation. Prior is PA and appears upright. Projection differs from the prior. Position and inspiration also differ, so comparison is limited.

LOOK AT FIRST:
- F1/F2: Increased bilateral hazy and reticular perihilar and mid zone opacity (both reads agree). Shortness of breath and SpO2 94 percent fit this pattern.
- F9: Linear densities over the tracheal air column, right upper mediastinum and upper abdomen that could be an endotracheal tube, an enteric tube or central line, or external tubing. Indeterminate. The two reads disagreed (read A indeterminate, read B new). Not present on the prior. Presence and tip positions are not confirmed.
- F3: Right basal opacity, indeterminate (both reads indeterminate, not comparable with the prior).
- F7: Enlarged cardiac silhouette, indeterminate for change (not time-sensitive, listed in look-first order).

FINDINGS (systematic read, done blind to the indication):
- Airway / lungs: Trachea roughly midline allowing for rotation. Lung volumes are low. Diffuse bilateral hazy and reticular opacity, most marked in the perihilar and mid zones, increased from the prior (F1 right, F2 left; both reads agree). Supine position and lower volumes contribute to part of the difference. This may reflect interstitial or alveolar fluid; other diffuse processes are not excluded. Denser opacity at both bases: right base (F3) and retrocardiac/left base (F4) are indeterminate and not comparable with the prior, because low volumes and supine position crowd the bases. No pleural line is seen, but pneumothorax cannot be excluded on a supine film. No discrete lung mass is seen, but the diffuse opacity, device generator and portable technique limit this.
- Mediastinum / hila: Both hila are indistinct with surrounding hazy opacity. The upper mediastinum looks wide on an AP supine film with mild rotation. Whether it is truly widened cannot be determined. See CAN'T DETERMINE.
- Pleura: Both costophrenic angles are hazy and both hemidiaphragms are partly obscured. Layering pleural effusions are possible on either side (F5 right, F6 left), indeterminate and not comparable with the upright prior. For each, only one of the two reads recorded the finding. Free gas under the diaphragm cannot be assessed on a supine film.
- Heart: Cardiac silhouette is enlarged on both studies (F7). It appears larger on the current film, but AP projection, supine position and low volumes magnify the heart shadow, so change is indeterminate. A left chest wall cardiac device generator with transvenous leads is present, with the same configuration as the prior allowing for projection (F8, stable). No visible lead discontinuity at this resolution.
- Bones / soft tissue: No displaced rib fracture or destructive bone lesion is seen at this resolution. No soft tissue gas. F10 (added in a focused pass, not seen in the blind reads): mottled, heterogeneous density projecting over the right glenoid and scapular neck region on the current film. It is indeterminate and not comparable with the prior. It could be projectional from arm position and the overlying ECG electrode, or altered bone texture. Review on the source images in PACS is needed.

INTERVAL CHANGE:
- Changed: Increased bilateral hazy and reticular perihilar and mid zone opacity (F1, F2), with supine position and low volumes contributing to part of the difference. Linear densities (F9) are not present on the prior, but their presence is indeterminate and the reads disagreed. Basal opacities, possible effusions, heart size, mediastinal width and F10 are not comparable across projections and position, so no change is reported for them.
- Unchanged: Left chest wall cardiac device generator and lead configuration (F8). No displaced rib fracture or destructive bone lesion on either study.

RECIST 1.1: Not computed on radiographs.

CAN'T DETERMINE:
- Has the heart size changed? | Reason: Prior is PA and current is AP supine with low volumes. AP projection and low inspiration magnify the heart shadow. | Recommend: Repeat PA and lateral when the patient is able. Echocardiography if clinically relevant.
- Is the upper mediastinum widened? | Reason: The current film is AP supine with mild rotation, which widens the mediastinal shadow. Device leads cross the region. | Recommend: Repeat upright PA film when the patient is able, or CT chest if there is clinical concern.
- Are pleural effusions present, and have they changed? | Reason: The current film is supine, so fluid layers posteriorly and shows only as haze. The prior is upright. The amounts are not comparable. | Recommend: Upright or decubitus film, bedside ultrasound, or CT chest.
- Do the basal opacities reflect consolidation, collapse, layering fluid or low volumes? | Reason: Low inspiration and supine position crowd the lower zones and mimic basal opacity. The magnified heart hides the left base. | Recommend: Repeat film with good inspiration when the patient is able, or CT chest.
- Is there a pneumothorax? | Reason: No pleural line is seen, but on a supine film air collects anteriorly and at the bases and may not show. A skin fold or linen line and external wires cross the chest. | Recommend: Upright or decubitus film, or CT chest if there is clinical concern.
- Are an endotracheal tube, enteric tube or central line present, and where are the tips? | Reason: Linear densities over the trachea, right upper mediastinum and upper abdomen overlap device leads, external wires and the spine. The image is low resolution. The reads disagreed on this finding. | Recommend: Review the source image in PACS with edge enhancement and correlate with the bedside record of lines and tubes. Confirm tip positions before use.
- Are there small lung nodules, or lesions behind the heart or generator? | Reason: Diffuse opacity on the current film, the device generator over the left upper chest and the enlarged heart all hide lung. The AP portable film is lower quality than the PA prior. | Recommend: CT chest if clinically relevant, or repeat PA and lateral after the diffuse opacity clears.
- Is there free gas under the diaphragm? | Reason: The current film is supine. Free gas does not collect under the diaphragm in this position. | Recommend: Upright or decubitus film if there is clinical concern.
- Is there a pleural effusion on either side, and has it changed? (read B wording) | Reason: The current film is supine, so fluid layers posteriorly and shows only as hazy density. Both costophrenic angles are indistinct on the current film and were clear on the upright PA prior. | Recommend: Upright or semi-erect film or decubitus views when the patient is able, or bedside ultrasound or CT chest.
- Is the upper mediastinum truly widened? (read B wording) | Reason: Supine AP projection with mild rotation widens the mediastinal shadow. The prior PA showed no widening. | Recommend: Repeat upright PA film when the patient is able, or CT chest if there is clinical concern.
- Is the right basal opacity consolidation, atelectasis or layering fluid? | Reason: Low lung volumes and supine position crowd the base and obscure the hemidiaphragm. A frontal film alone cannot separate these. | Recommend: Repeat film with better inspiration, upright if possible, or CT chest.
- Where exactly is the endotracheal tube tip relative to the carina, and is there an enteric tube with its tip in the stomach? (read B wording; presence of either tube is itself unconfirmed and the reads disagreed) | Reason: The image is low resolution and the carina is not clearly defined. A tubular density over the upper abdomen could be an enteric tube or external tubing. | Recommend: Review the source image in PACS with windowing. Repeat the film if the tube positions remain unclear.
- Are there small nodules or subtle bone lesions on either study? | Reason: The device generator overlies the left upper and mid zones on both films. Diffuse opacity and portable technique on the current film hide fine detail. | Recommend: CT chest if clinically indicated. Review source images in PACS.

IMPRESSION:
1. Increased bilateral hazy and reticular perihilar and mid zone opacity compared with the prior (F1, F2; both reads agree). This may reflect interstitial or alveolar fluid; other diffuse processes are not excluded. Supine position and low volumes contribute to part of the difference.
2. Linear densities over the trachea, right upper mediastinum and upper abdomen (F9) are indeterminate. The reads disagreed. They could be an endotracheal tube, an enteric tube or central line, or external tubing. Presence and tip positions are not confirmed.
3. Bibasal opacities (right F3, left F4) are indeterminate and not comparable with the prior. Consolidation, collapse, layering fluid and low volumes cannot be separated.
4. Enlarged cardiac silhouette on both studies (F7). Change is indeterminate across PA and AP supine projections.
5. Possible pleural effusions (F5, F6) are indeterminate. Pneumothorax and free gas are not excluded on this supine film. Upper mediastinal width cannot be judged.
6. Mottled density over the right glenoid and scapular neck region (F10) is indeterminate, in a patient with a history of prostate cancer. It needs review on the source images in PACS.
7. Left chest wall cardiac device and leads are stable in configuration compared with the prior (F8).

RECOMMENDATIONS:
- Repeat PA and lateral chest radiograph, upright with good inspiration, when the patient is able.
- Upright or decubitus film, bedside ultrasound, or CT chest for effusion, pneumothorax and basal opacity if there is clinical concern.
- CT chest if clinically relevant for small nodules, lesions behind the heart or generator, or mediastinal width.
- Echocardiography if clinically relevant for heart size.
- Review source images in PACS for tube and line positions, lead integrity and the right scapular density (F10). Correlate with the bedside record of lines and tubes and confirm tip positions before use.

AI DRAFT: requires resident review and attending signature.
